hook.en: An assessment system that uses how symptoms respond to repeated movements to guide a self-management exercise plan.
hook.ur: McKenzie MDT ek assessment aur self-management system hai jo repeated movements ya sustained positions ke baad symptoms ki tabdeeli dekh kar exercises choose karta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what McKenzie Method — Mechanical Diagnosis & Therapy (MDT) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (4 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke McKenzie Method — Mechanical Diagnosis & Therapy (MDT) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 4 checks.)

text.en: McKenzie Mechanical Diagnosis and Therapy (MDT) is mostly active care. You test repeated movements or sustained positions, watch how pain moves, and use the response to classify the problem and choose exercises the patient does themselves.
text.ur: MDT zyada tar active care hai. Clinician repeated movements ya sustained positions test karta hai, pain ki location aur response dekhta hai, phir pattern classify karke patient ko khud karne wali exercises sikhata hai.

simpler.en: An assessment system that uses how symptoms respond to repeated movements to guide a self-management exercise plan.
simpler.ur: McKenzie MDT ek assessment aur self-management system hai jo repeated movements ya sustained positions ke baad symptoms ki tabdeeli dekh kar exercises choose karta hai.

text.en: Like a compass for movement: the pain's behavior points toward the direction that helps, rather than assuming one exercise suits everyone.
text.ur: Yeh movement ka compass hai: symptoms ka rawaiya us direction ki taraf ishara karta hai jo madad kare, bajaye is ke ke har shakhs ko ek hi exercise di jaye.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Directional preference: some people improve with a repeated movement direction (often extension), others with flexion or sideways movements.
**2.** Centralization: pain moving from the leg toward the spine during testing is a good sign; peripheralization (moving away) is a warning.
**3.** The patient learns to manage symptoms themselves, with minimal dependence on hands-on treatment.
text.ur: Directional preference: kuch log repeated extension se behtar hote hain, kuch flexion ya side movement se. Centralization: test ke dauran limb ka dard spine ki taraf wapas aaye to yeh favorable response ho sakta hai. Peripheralization: symptoms limb mein aur door chale jayein to yeh warning hai. Patient ko self-management sikhana central feature hai.

question.en: Vocabulary first — clinicians use this word a lot. What does **Centralization** mean?
question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **Centralization** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en: Symptoms moving farther down the limb.
text.ur: Symptoms moving farther down the limb.

text.en:
So when does **McKenzie Method — Mechanical Diagnosis & Therapy (MDT)** make sense?
• Back or neck pain, with or without arm or leg pain, with no red flags.
• When you want the patient to take charge of treatment.
text.ur: Red flags ke baghair back/neck pain, arm ya leg pain ke sath bhi, aur jab patient ko self-management dena maqsad ho. Progressive weakness, bowel/bladder control ka loss, saddle numbness, major trauma ya systemic illness mein urgent medical review chahiye. Testing se symptoms peripheralize hon ya neurological signs barhein to us direction ko continue na karein.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Red flags: progressive weakness, loss of bowel or bladder control, saddle numbness, major trauma or systemic illness.
• When symptoms peripheralize or neurological signs worsen during testing.
**Stop rule:** Stop and seek appropriate evaluation for progressive weakness, bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle symptoms, major trauma or other concerning neurologic changes.
text.ur:
Utna hi zaroori — kab yeh technique NAHI karni, ya kab ruk jana hai:
• Red flags: progressive weakness, loss of bowel or bladder control, saddle numbness, major trauma or systemic illness.
• When symptoms peripheralize or neurological signs worsen during testing.
**Stop rule:** Stop and seek appropriate evaluation for progressive weakness, bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle symptoms, major trauma or other concerning neurologic changes.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Draw a symptom map
steps.detail: Record where symptoms are, which is the farthest, and daily-task limits.

steps.title: Screen
steps.detail: Rule out red flags and check neurological status.

steps.title: Test repeated movements
steps.detail: Example: repeated extension in lying for about 10 repetitions.

steps.title: Watch the response
steps.detail: Note location, intensity and after-effects. Does leg pain retreat toward the back?

steps.title: Classify and prescribe
steps.detail: If a direction helps, teach it as a home exercise; if not, test another.

steps.title: Review across visits
steps.detail: Recheck symptom map, function and neurological status.

beats.ur:
1. Symptom map banayein: jagah, sab se door symptom aur daily-task limits.
2. Red flags aur neurological status screen karein.
3. Repeated movements test karein; example ke taur par lying mein extension ke takreeban 10 reps.
4. Location, intensity aur baad ke effects note karein: kya leg pain back ki taraf retreat karta hai?
5. Helpful direction ho to home exercise sikhayein; warna doosri direction assess karein.
6. Visits ke darmiyan symptom map, function aur neurological status dobara check karein.

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: about 10 repetitions of the helpful movement, repeated several times a day while symptoms are active, adjusted by a trained clinician.
text.ur: Teaching mein helpful movement ke takreeban 10 reps din mein kai martaba diye ja sakte hain jab symptoms active hon, magar trained clinician response ke mutabiq adjust kare.

beats.patient: Carlos, 41, driver, low back pain and calf pain after sitting.
beats.assessment: Repeated extension in lying makes the calf pain retreat to the buttock; flexion makes it worse.
beats.treatment: He is taught extension in lying, 10 repetitions every few hours, and posture advice for driving.
beats.reassess: Calf pain is gone after a week and walking improves. If it had worsened or weakness appeared, the plan would change.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Source mein Carlos, 41 saal ke driver, ko sitting ke baad low-back aur calf pain hai. Lying mein repeated extension se calf pain buttock ki taraf retreat karta hai, jabke flexion se barhta hai. Use extension exercise aur driving posture advice sikhayi jati hai; follow-up mein calf pain khatam aur walking behtar hoti hai. Symptoms barhte ya weakness aati to plan badalta. Yeh teaching scenario hai, prescription nahi.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Giving extension to everyone.
• Continuing when symptoms peripheralize.
• Declaring a disc has been 'put back'.
**Myth to drop:** 'McKenzie means back extensions for everyone.' It actually means individualized mechanical assessment and classification.
text.ur: Har patient ko extension dena; symptoms peripheralize hone par bhi continue karna; ya kehna ke disc ko 'wapis jagah par' rakh diya gaya.

text.en:
MDT has research as an assessment and self-management system, with benefits depending on the condition and comparison. Directional preference and centralization are recognized patterns, though they do not prove a disc moved.
MDT has a body of research as an assessment and management system; outcomes are condition- and subgroup-dependent. Avoid claiming that any one exercise fixes all discs.
